> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/objectql/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8a7437e95e190c8107a029cad331b9b35aeba7f` — the merge of head `9931bb55d34e72a9d0fc784dcba2d59dbc94f89d` into base `e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8a7437e95e190c8107a029cad331b9b35aeba7f && git checkout c8a7437e95e190c8107a029cad331b9b35aeba7f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182 9931bb55d34e72a9d0fc784dcba2d59dbc94f89d && git checkout -B drift-repro e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182 && git merge --no-ff 9931bb55d34e72a9d0fc784dcba2d59dbc94f89d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e250d8f84b2fb154692715a066a95a4f00cbd182` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9931bb55d34e72a9d0fc784dcba2d59dbc94f89d`
Local-runs: none

Reading time 2026-10-10T15:30Z. Read-only throughout: card #22637 (body; triage 6095345451; claim 6097826006; os-dev-report 6098964328), decision card #22624 and ruling 6094990917, ADR-0104 D3 on `main`, the cross-lane declarations 6097907456 (#6021) and 6098008938 (#6023), PR #22697 (body, file list, and the compare diff of the head against `main`, merge-base `d973c34cdd`), the head's check-runs, and the source at the head and at the merge-base through the REST API plus a blobless scratch clone under this seat's scratch space (a read; nothing was built, run, re-run or ablated here).

**Gate verdicts on the head.** 35 check-runs, all concluded: 33 `success`, 2 `skipped` (Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke, both opt-in or path-scheduled). All seven required contexts are `success`: Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Dogfood Regression Gate, Build Core, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Governed Surface Queue Guard. The file list (8 paths) touches no governed surface; head repo equals base repo; 1,316 changed lines.

### ① Derived judgments

Each item names what the diff implies and whether it is right against the ruling's words (a refused reader is served the metadata of a file whose `ref_object` / `ref_id` name the record being read, by the download door's own parent-derived verdict, the delegate consulted where the owner object declares `fileAccessDelegate`; every other id keeps PR #22620's marker; direct `sys_file` queries and `public_read` unchanged; no second predicate) and ADR-0104 D3 ("field-referenced files get parent-derived read checks, reusing the attachments `authorizeFileRead` verdict model"; the expanded form "produced at read/expand time from the `sys_file` row").

1. **The engine's refused arm and its system-context `sys_file` read: RIGHT.** On `isReadRefusal` only (the `PERMISSION_DENIED` code; a database ACL fault still takes the outage arm), `readParentDerivedFiles` makes one `sys_file` read under `{ ...caller, isSystem: true }`, the exact shape of `ScopedContext.sudo()` in `engine.ts`, so the caller's `tenantId` (the driver tenant scope in `buildDriverOptions`) and transaction ride along and the security layer's explicit system opt-in short-circuits the CRUD gate (`security-plugin.ts`, the "explicit system opt-in" predicate). Its `where` is the ownership pair itself (`id $in` the ids the result holds, `ref_object` this object, `ref_id $in` this result's record ids) and it projects seven columns (`PARENT_DERIVED_FILE_COLUMNS`), so a file not field-owned by a record in the result is never read. The caller's envelope is forwarded to the verdict stripped of `__` keys (`withoutOperationPrivateKeys`, core). The rows the verdict allows go through the one servability rule (`servableFileRows`, extracted from the normal arm unchanged) and the one renderer (`toFileValue`, the former inline `toValue`), so both arms hand out one shape. Failure of the system read or of the verdict: every id keeps the marker, the record read still succeeds, one `warn` (functional degradation; `check:durability-log-level` green). Pinned: the system read happens once, its `where` carries the pair, the verdict is asked once with owner ids only and no `__` key, the failing-read and throwing-verdict cases keep the marker with one `warn`. Observation, not a defect: a principal-less context (refused by the security layer for carrying no principal) reaches this arm, performs the system read, and the verdict then returns nothing because the envelope has no `userId`; the read's result is discarded. Cost only, nothing served.
2. **The ownership match is the ruling's scope condition, not a second predicate: RIGHT.** The ruling itself reduces the verdict at hydration to "the file's reference points at this record, with the delegate consulted where declared". The engine copies no access rule: the `where` and the per-row `ref_object` / `ref_id` re-check select WHICH ids are put to the verdict; allow and deny, delegate and fail-closed included, come from the storage package's function. The non-delegate arm re-reads the owner record as the caller, which the ruling says reduces to the read already made; the dev kept the door's own call instead of short-cutting it, which is one predicate applied unchanged, and the redundancy is named in the acceptance notes.
3. **The seam `registerFieldOwnedFileReadAuthorizer` and the exported type `FieldOwnedFileReadAuthorizer`: RIGHT.** The engine declares the shape (owner object, owner ids, context, returning the readable subset) and never implements it; `StorageServicePlugin.start()` fills it beside `registerHeldFileResolver`, duck-typed so an older engine keeps the marker; last registration wins; the storage function is module-private (no `export`). The engine package gains one public method and one exported type (`index.ts`), nothing else on its surface. `ObjectQL` holds no service registry, so this handover is the way to reach a declared `fileAccessDelegate` without a copy.
4. **`readableFieldOwners`: the door's verdict is byte-for-byte unchanged for every request, delegate and fail-closed paths included: RIGHT, verified against the merge-base source.** The door's field-owned arm now calls it with the one owner id. Four textual differences exist and none changes a reachable verdict: (a) `where: { id: ownerIds[0] }` where `ownerIds[0]` is `String(file.ref_id)`, against the old `where: { id: file.ref_id }`; `sys_file.ref_id` is a `text` column and `FileRecord.ref_id` is `string | null`, so the value is identical; (b) the new `userId` guard returns the empty set, and the door already answers `'unauthenticated'` before this arm when `authz.userId` is absent, so the guard is dead for the door and only binds the hydration caller, in the door's own direction; (c) `limit: ownerIds.length` is `1` for the door; (d) the delegate's `getService` throw, a missing or non-function delegate, a falsy answer and a thrown `authorizeFileRead` each deny, exactly as the single `try` did. The owner arm (uploader allowed) and the attachment-parent arm are untouched; `storage-routes.ts` (`authorizeDownload`, the `public_read` carve-out) is not in the diff. The door's existing tests are unedited and Test Core is green on the head; the new agreement test asks the real door (`GET /files/:fileId/url`) and the real record read about one SqlDriver fixture with the plugin booted as it ships.
5. **The unwired engine keeps the marker: RIGHT.** `readParentDerivedFiles` returns before any read when no authorizer is registered; pinned (every id refused, zero system reads). The unedited plugin-security pin (`file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts`, real `SecurityPlugin`, no storage plugin) is that engine and stays green.
6. **`multiple` fields and mixed arrays: RIGHT.** Judged per element and per record: an owned id hydrates on its owner only, the same id copied into another record of the same object keeps the marker there, an id owned by a record of another object with the same id keeps the marker, a copied, attachment-only or `public_read` element keeps the marker, a legacy URL element passes through. Pinned in both test files (`gallery` of four; `annexes` of five).
7. **Nothing widens `sys_file`'s own read rule, a direct `sys_file` query, or `public_read`: RIGHT.** The caller's own `sys_file` read is the unchanged first read and is still refused; the system read is engine-internal, scoped to the ownership pair, and nothing it reads reaches the caller unless the door's verdict allows the owner; a direct `sys_file` query by the refused reader is pinned `PERMISSION_DENIED` 403 in both test files; `public_read` is pinned anonymous 200 at the door and the marker in the refused read for a `public_read` file the record does not own. A `public_read` file the record does own hydrates by the verdict, which is the ruling's rule, not a change to `public_read`.
8. **An owned, allowed row that is not servable reads as the bare id: RIGHT, noted.** A pending upload and an unheld tombstone read for the refused reader exactly as they read for a `sys_file` reader (pinned against the system read). The ruling serves "exactly as a `sys_file` reader" and servability is not an access verdict; the types.mdx edit keeps the bare id's documented meaning (not provisioned, or an outage).
9. **Re-entry terminates.** The verdict's owner re-read is projected to `fields: ['id']`, so its result carries no file field and `resolveFileReferences` returns before any `sys_file` read (the engine planner keeps `id` in a projection; the memory driver's `projectFields` and SqlDriver honour `fields`). The shipped delegate (`approvals`) reads the action under its own system context with `fields: ['request_id']` and the request as the caller, and `sys_approval_request` declares no media field (its `attachments` are action params), so a delegate-governed refused read makes no unbounded loop.
10. **Docs: RIGHT.** Two hand-written passages (`protocol/objectql/types.mdx` file read forms; `permissions/attachments-access.mdx` refused-reader clause) gain the parent-derived case, prose only; no generated page, no `content/docs/releases/` path.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/22637-file-field-metadata-parent-derived.md`: `@objectstack/objectql: minor`, `@objectstack/service-storage: minor`, body carries `Clause-②: yes`, no ADR-0087 marker (nothing an author writes is removed or renamed; not breaking). That matches what the diff publishes: objectql gains a public method, an exported type and the widened read; service-storage gains the engine registration and a verdict-preserving extraction. The two docs files publish nothing; `packages/spec` is untouched, so no spec changeset and no regenerated artifact is owed. `Clause-②: yes` stands on the PR body, the changeset and the card, and is right: a widening of what a refused reader is served; `yes` takes at least `minor`, satisfied. No `skip-changeset`. Check Changeset, `check:adr-0087-registration` and `check:empty-changeset` are green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations, each answered:
- Cross-lane edits beyond `packages/objectql`: declared before any edit, verified on the timeline. The `domain:services` declaration landed at 2026-10-10T13:18Z and the first `service-storage` commit (`4525b2e2d5`) at 2026-10-10T13:31Z; the `domain:devx` declaration at 2026-10-10T13:30Z and the docs commit (`1932869678`) at 2026-10-10T13:32Z. The declared paths are exactly the paths edited (two `service-storage` files; two docs files). Answered.
- Two first-pass gate reds from the dev's own test code, fixed: Lint & Repo Gates is `success` on the head. Answered.
- `origin/main` merged before pr_create: `main` has since moved 9 commits past the merge-base; none touches `packages/objectql`, `packages/services/service-storage`, `packages/core/src/security` or the two docs; the one `plugin-security` source change (`security-plugin.ts`, +20/-1, capability declarations) does not touch the system opt-in or the `sys_file` gate. The queue's rebuild covers the merge commit. Answered.
- Foreground CI polling: logistics only. Answered.

`out_of_scope_findings`, each answered or escalated:
- **Spec TSDoc now incomplete (`FileRefusedValueSchema`; `fileAccessDelegate` TSDoc and `.describe()`): ESCALATED to the dispatching seat, as a filed card, not a note.** `FileRefusedValueSchema` still says "Nothing else is served, because nothing else was read"; after this PR the marker also means "the parent-derived verdict did not allow", and for an owned, verdict-refused file the engine did read the row. `fileAccessDelegate`'s `.describe()` ("authorizes downloads of files owned by this object's media fields") now undersells the delegate: it is also asked, once per owner, on every refused record read of a delegate-governed object, with the caller's execution context. That text is what an author reads when declaring the delegate, so under Prime Directive 10 it is a metadata-authoring trap to file, and the fix is a `.describe()` change plus `gen:schema`, `gen:docs` in `domain:spec`, correctly left out of this diff. It does not make this PR wrong. Seat action: file the `domain:spec` card (dedupe words as the report gives them).
- **No committed full-composition pin (real `SecurityPlugin` + `StorageServicePlugin` + REST): ANSWERED, accepted.** The committed pins cover the engine's half (fake driver, recorded verdict) and the door agreement (real engine, SqlDriver, the real plugin, stand-in refusal of the measured shape); the one fact only the scratch run measured, that the sudo-shaped read passes the real CRUD gate, holds by reading of the security plugin's system opt-in. A `packages/qa` dogfood pin is `domain:cli` and optional; not a merge condition.
- **Narrower than the door for an uploader whose delegate refuses them: ANSWERED, within the ruling.** The ruling cites the field-owned arm (`:1237-:1265`) by name, and the owner arm precedes it; the hydration being narrower there is the ruling as written, not a deviation. Widening to the owner arm would be a new decision card, not this PR's defect.

Nothing else in the diff falls outside the card's scope. The PR is a draft; after this record the owning seat flips it ready and arms auto-merge on green.

Reviewed-by: `session_01Bw3y2DWhT9RPnrmDsNqEVG`
